triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '14. Direct global V for RHS is slower than cp.async staging' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 14. Direct global V for RHS is slower than cp.async staging

problem.statement: GDN Chunk Forward Pitfalls (CuTeDSL, SM120) -- 14. Direct global V for RHS is slower than cp.async staging

payload.attempted: After removing the dead `v_new -> sV` store, original V is only used once to build RHS. It is tempting to skip `mV -> sV` cp.async and read `gV_tile[row, v]` directly inside the RHS R2S loop.
payload.lesson: "One-use" does not automatically mean "load directly from global." In this GDN K1, keep V cp.async staging unless the direct path is vectorized and ncu proves lower long-scoreboard / global-sector cost.

established_fact.mechanism: The CuTeDSL scalar `gV_tile[row, v_col]` access was not a vectorized `CopyUniversalOp` load. It inserted scalar global loads on the RHS critical path (`LDG.E.U16` rose) while removing only a small amount of shared-load work. cp.async V staging remained better because it coalesces and overlaps the load before the RHS dependency chain.

payload.observed: Correct but slower. V30 repeat-100 regressed to `0.7200 ms` vs V29 `0.6861 ms`; ncu K1 regressed to `743.58 us` vs `706.40 us`.
payload.root_cause: The CuTeDSL scalar `gV_tile[row, v_col]` access was not a vectorized `CopyUniversalOp` load. It inserted scalar global loads on the RHS critical path (`LDG.E.U16` rose) while removing only a small amount of shared-load work. cp.async V staging remained better because it coalesces and overlaps the load before the RHS dependency chain.
